concepts.preferred_label: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
support_spans: NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
concepts.why: The patient has a history of NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and the echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 25% with global hypokinesis.

support_spans: delta wave present in QRS complex B
concepts.why: The ECG shows alternating QRS complex morphologies with a delta wave, which is characteristic of Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome.
The patient has mild wheezing and an elevated brain natriuretic peptide level, which could be indicative of pulmonary hypertension, but the chest radiograph shows no acute cardiopulmonary processes.
The patient has a history of polysubstance abuse and a reduced ejection fraction with global hypokinesis, which could be indicative of cardiomyopathy induced by substance abuse.

support_spans: bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema for 10 days
concepts.why: The patient presents with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, which could be indicative of nephrotic syndrome.
The combination of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, absence of acute cardiopulmonary processes on chest radiograph, and elevated troponin levels may indicate cardiac amyloidosis.
The presence of sinus tachycardia at a rate of 100 and the delta wave in QRS complex B on the ECG suggest atrial fibrillation with pre-excitation, which is not fully explained by the existing labels.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of alternating QRS complex morphologies and a delta wave in QRS complex B specifically supports Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome.
